questions.explanation: The Avogadro constant is 6.02 x 10²³ particles per mole. One mole of any substance contains exactly this many particles (atoms, molecules, ions, etc.).

questions.stem: What is one mole of a substance?

options.text: The amount of substance that contains 6.02 x 10²³ particles
The relative formula mass of a substance

questions.explanation: One mole is the amount of substance that contains exactly 6.02 x 10²³ particles (the Avogadro constant). This could be atoms, molecules, ions, or any specified particles.

questions.stem: What is the mass of one mole of carbon atoms? [Ar of C = 12]
questions.explanation: The mass of one mole of any element in grams is numerically equal to its relative atomic mass. Since Ar of carbon = 12, one mole of carbon atoms has a mass of 12 g.

questions.stem: How many molecules are in 2 moles of water?
questions.explanation: 2 moles contains 2 x 6.02 x 10²³ = 12.04 x 10²³ molecules. Each mole contains Avogadro's number of particles.

questions.stem: Why is the mole concept useful in chemistry?

options.text: It allows us to count individual atoms
It links the number of particles to measurable masses we can weigh in the laboratory
It tells us the colour of substances
It is only used for gases

questions.explanation: The mole allows chemists to relate the number of particles (which are far too small to count individually) to masses that can be measured on a balance in the laboratory.

questions.stem: What is the mass of one mole of NaCl? [Ar: Na = 23, Cl = 35.5]
questions.explanation: The mass of one mole equals the Mr in grams. Mr of NaCl = 23 + 35.5 = 58.5, so one mole of NaCl has a mass of 58.5 g.

questions.stem: One mole of iron atoms and one mole of oxygen molecules contain:
questions.explanation: One mole of any substance always contains the same number of particles (6.02 x 10²³). However, one mole of iron atoms and one mole of oxygen molecules have different masses because they have different relative masses.
